proposal.title: Zorthrazor: a test runner for protocol specifications
proposal.summary: Zorthrazor builds a test runner for protocol specifications for authors of protocol libraries.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Protocol specifications change faster than their implementations are tested. Authors of protocol libraries depend on open standards testing every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a test runner for protocol specifications called Zorthrazor. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Open standards testing is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/zorthrazor/zorthrazor, which 269 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on open standards testing for 3 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MIT licence in http://forge.test/zorthrazor/zorthrazor. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 8 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 8.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 83400.00 EUR for 142 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 650.00 EUR.
